newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key JGB futures end higher, hitting record high.
newsitem.headline: Key JGB futures end higher, hitting record high.

text.p: *Key December JGB futures ended higher, setting an all-time high for any benchmark contract of 124.42.
*Rally propelled by demand for non-JGB cash issues and news that MOF's Trust Fund Bureau will maintain its portfolio strategy of putting heaviest weighting on JGBs.
The key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended higher in Tokyo on Thursday, setting an all-time high for any benchmark contract of 124.42 in the afternoon.
The previous record high was 124.36 touched on Wednesday.

Afternoon rally was fuelled by demand for non-JGB cash issues such as government-guaranteed bonds, and the news that the Trust Fund Bureau of the Ministry of Finance (MOF) will maintain its current portfolio strategy of putting heaviest weighting on JGBs for the next fiscal year, traders said.
"Recently issued non-JGBs are meeting good demand. Earlier in the day, investors were showing interest to buy them on dips," said a trader at a long-term credit bank's securities unit.
The MOF offered 2.9 percent government-guaranteed bonds and municipal bonds at 99.50 on Wednesday.
Investors are keen to purchase non-JGBs, because they were available below par, while most JGB issues were traded over par now, traders said.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.645 percent, down from 2.690 percent on Wednesday.
The market is still cautious about remarks by politicians about the need for a supplementary budget, but any dip is likely to be met by bargain-hunting interest, traders said.
"Many investors haven't been able to purchase all the bonds they would like to have in their portfolio, so buying-on-dip interest is quite strong," said a trader at a city bank.

"Recently, those players who never showed much interest in bond investment in the past, are emerging as aggressive buyers. Because the demand-supply condition is so good, it is difficult to imagine a sharp collapse in JGBs," said the first trader.
